name: Viktor
notes: Opens with Arcane Storm at t=0 for its initial burst, then lets the singularity tick on the dummy roughly once per second for the rest of its base duration (7 total damage instances: the initial burst plus 6 subsequent ticks, matching the wiki's explicit '7 strikes' and the bin's MaxTicks=6 read as the count of subsequent ticks only).

Siphon Power is cast on cooldown; it deals its missile damage and grants Discharge for 4 seconds, read here as applying unconditionally on cast (not gated on the missile landing) since the two readings only differ by the missile's negligible travel time.

The next basic attack after Discharge is armed is converted: it deals no normal attack damage and instead deals Discharge's modified magic damage (base + 100% total AD + 50% AP) as a separate, non-crit instance, per the wiki's note that Discharge disables bonus crit damage and replaces the normal on-hit with the modified magic damage.
If no attack lands within Discharge's 4 second window it expires unused; this should not happen at typical level-16 attack speeds but is modeled with an expiry event to be safe.
Hextech Ray has no cast time and is cast on cooldown, its damage applied on cast since it has no meaningful delay before landing on a stationary target and Viktor can freely act while it travels.
Gravity Field is never cast: it deals no damage, and its slow/stun (crowd control on a target that never moves or acts) has no effect in this fight.
Arcane Storm's cooldown starts post-effect (after the ~6.5 s storm ends) and is 80-120 s even at max rank, so it is cast exactly once inside any fight length modeled here.
Mana costs are not modeled: nothing here would actually stall casts within a 15 s window at level 16.

assumed.why: Hextech Ray's short travel time to a stationary dummy is not modeled as a delay; its damage is applied on cast.
